description: A standalone Windows desktop (WinForms) application for managing student academic records. A dashboard form summarizes student counts by gender, course, and academic year, and three companion forms let a user insert, view/search, edit, and delete individual student records (name, course, year of admission, gender, mobile numbers, date of birth), all persisted to a local Microsoft Access database file bundled in the repository. The author's own README and project report describe it as a single-developer academic/portfolio project with no network, web, or batch component.

architecture.archetype_rationale: Evidence: OutputType=WinExe and MyType=WindowsForms in the .vbproj; four Form classes (Form1 dashboard, InsertForm, EditForm, ViewForm) wired together via Windows Forms controls and panel-swapping, not HTTP routes; all data access is direct OleDb SQL (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against a single 'students' table) against a local .accdb file opened via a hardcoded file-system path in Module1.vb — no listener, no scheduler entry point, no API surface. This does not cleanly map to any option in the suggested taxonomy (web-app, batch, hybrid, service, headless, cli, library, mainframe, embedded): it is not web-app (no HTTP server/templates), not headless (it has a GUI), not batch/scheduled (interactive, user-driven), not cli/library/mainframe/embedded. 'desktop' is used here as the closest accurate label for a standalone GUI thick-client bound to a local file database; flagged in open_questions as a taxonomy gap.
architecture.major_components_note: Single WinForms project ('Flat Design') with one dashboard form (Form1) that hosts three child forms (InsertForm, EditForm, ViewForm) in a panel; a Module1.vb holds the single shared OleDbConnection; data layer is inline SQL in each form, no DAL/service layer, no ORM.

size_metrics.loc_excluded_vendor_note: No files were excluded from the count. Of the 2,787 total .vb lines, approximately 2,326 lines (83%) are WinForms Designer-generated layout code (*.Designer.vb, Resources.Designer.vb, Settings.Designer.vb, Application.Designer.vb) and approximately 461 lines (17%) are hand-written form/business logic (Form1.vb, InsertForm.vb, EditForm.vb, ViewForm.vb, Module1.vb, AssemblyInfo.vb).
size_metrics.module_count_basis: Single .vbproj ('Student Management System Siddharth Jain.vbproj', WinForms desktop project) under the 'Flat Design' directory. The source tree has no further package/module decomposition (no sub-projects, no class library split).
size_metrics.endpoint_count_basis: Not applicable. This is a standalone WinForms desktop application with no HTTP listener, REST endpoint, or RPC surface; all interaction is local GUI event handlers against a local MS Access database.
size_metrics.table_count_note: Only one table, 'students', is referenced by every SQL statement found across the four forms (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on columns rollno, fname, lname, fathername, mobno, altmobno, gender, course, yoa, dob). The actual studentDB.accdb file is a binary MS Access database and could not be parsed directly with text tooling, so this count is inferred from embedded SQL text, not from DDL; Pass 1 (Structural Analysis) should confirm against the real .accdb schema.

open_questions: Governing client profile for this task is 'faa' (FAA legacy modernization program, per profiles/faa/profile.yaml: NAS safety, air traffic, pilot certification, etc.), but this application's source, README, and project report describe a generic student-record-management desktop tool with no detectable aviation, NAS, or FAA business relevance. This is a likely scope/profile mismatch and should be confirmed by the engagement owner before this catalog entry is used for FAA-specific gating (safety tiering, NAS impact assessment, compliance mapping).

safety_tier could not be set: no authoritative safety classification input was provided at onboarding or by a prior Discovery run. Per methodology, safety tier must come from stakeholder/Safety Board input, not be inferred from code. For reference only: the FAA profile README's qualitative signal table (profiles/faa/README.md) would suggest a 'T3' lean for an 'Admin'-domain application with no external interfaces and a small user base, but this is not a substitute for authoritative classification.

business_domain was set to 'Admin' as the closest general match from the FAA profile's documented domain taxonomy (Air Traffic, Flight Safety, Aviation Safety, Certification, Workforce, Finance, Admin, Travel, Timesheet — profiles/faa/README.md), because neither the repository nor its docs state an actual business owner, sponsoring office, or domain, and the application itself does not resemble an FAA system. Needs stakeholder confirmation.
No CMDB export or ownership/criticality documentation was provided at onboarding; business owner and operational criticality are unconfirmed.

fixtures/default.json, found inside this application's own source tree, is a QA/test fixture for the catalog-application skill itself (its 'result' payload describes an unrelated fictitious 'Fixture Application' with a C#/ASP.NET WebForms/SQL Server stack). It was disregarded as a source of facts about this application. Its presence inside the real application's source tree (rather than in test infrastructure) may be worth investigating upstream, since it could indicate repository/fixture cross-contamination.

The active FAA profile's legacy-technology mapping (profiles/faa/technology.yaml, modernization_targets.dotnet) only covers ASP.NET/C#/WCF; it defines no modernization target for a VB.NET WinForms + MS Access desktop stack, so no profile-driven replatform/rehost target currently applies to this application.

Archetype taxonomy gap: the archetype enum suggested for this artifact (web-app, batch, hybrid, service, headless, cli, library, mainframe, embedded) has no category for a standalone GUI desktop/thick-client application; 'desktop' was used as the closest accurate label. Recommend the taxonomy owner add an explicit desktop/thick-client archetype.
